label: copy-phase input w when the next output is w or n (late in sequence)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and essentially only when the fed-back input token is w (2702/2704 dev activations). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Among copy-phase w inputs, it fires mostly when the token to emit next (the original token after w) is w or n (about 93% of activation mass), with a weaker tail for u. It favors later positions (recall_idx >= 3) and the last few outputs (to_go 0-2). The strongest activations are on a w that follows an earlier copied p/1/f and is followed by w or n in the original, near the end of the sequence. Precision is limited: many copy-phase w->w/n steps do not fire at all, and this is not explained by position, to_go or the previous token. The bare condition copy-phase in_tok == w has recall 0.999 but precision 0.03.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, n, -, r, 2, k; least: x, o, e, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: w, n, u, o, s, a; least: y, t, 3, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=5, L=4 & t=6.
